If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We’re building a next-generation ambient AI platform for healthcare, helping clinicians focus on patient care by automatically capturing, understanding, and structuring clinical conversations.

Behind that experience is a distributed system responsible for ingesting long-form audio, processing real-time and asynchronous streams, orchestrating multiple AI models, and reliably producing clinical outputs. These workflows must remain observable and recoverable across network interruptions, partial failures, model timeouts, and rapidly changing inference infrastructure.

We’re hiring a Backend Engineer to help build and operate this foundation. You’ll work across audio ingestion, media processing, inference orchestration, distributed workflows, storage, observability, and cloud infrastructure.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys making complex systems dependable. You think carefully about failure modes, idempotency, backpressure, data integrity, latency, and operational simplicity. You also understand that infrastructure exists to serve the product: the systems you build must ultimately create a fast, reliable, and trustworthy experience for clinicians.

What You’ll Do

  • Design, build, and operate backend systems that power our Ambient AI products across mobile and web.

  • Own critical parts of the audio processing lifecycle, including:

    • Real-time and asynchronous audio ingestion

    • Streaming and chunked uploads

    • Audio validation, encoding, normalization, and processing

    • Durable storage and media lifecycle management

    • Recovery from interrupted, duplicated, delayed, or out-of-order uploads

  • Build and evolve inference workflows that coordinate transcription, diarization, language models, clinical extraction, summarization, and other AI capabilities.

  • Develop orchestration systems for long-running, multi-stage workflows, including:

    • Scheduling, queueing, and workload prioritization

    • Retries, timeouts, fallbacks, and dead-letter handling

    • Idempotency, replay, and safe workflow recovery

    • Model routing, versioning, and configuration

    • Progress tracking and user-visible workflow state

    • Graceful degradation when dependencies are unavailable

  • Improve the reliability and scalability of services operating under variable, compute-intensive workloads.

  • Define and maintain service-level objectives for critical workflows, including availability, processing latency, completion rates, and data durability.

  • Build strong observability across services and pipelines through structured logging, metrics, distributed tracing, dashboards, alerting, and diagnostic tooling.

  • Lead incident response and post-incident analysis for important production failures, turning operational lessons into lasting improvements.

  • Identify systemic failure patterns and eliminate them through better abstractions, automation, testing, and architecture.

  • Improve cloud infrastructure, deployment systems, capacity planning, and operational tooling as the platform scales.

  • Design APIs and data models that allow mobile, web, and internal systems to interact with long-running workflows safely and predictably.

  • Build tools that make inference pipelines easier to inspect, test, replay, evaluate, and debug.

  • Balance reliability, latency, quality, and infrastructure cost across AI and media-processing workloads.

  • Partner closely with mobile, product, AI, security, and clinical teams to turn new capabilities into production-ready workflows.

  • Mentor other engineers and help establish strong practices for distributed systems, observability, operational readiness, and backend architecture.

What You Have

  • 4+ years of professional backend or infrastructure engineering experience.

  • Experience designing, building, and operating production distributed systems.

  • Strong proficiency in at least one modern backend programming language.

  • Experience with asynchronous processing, message queues, event-driven systems, or durable workflow execution.

About the Role

We’re building a next-generation ambient AI platform for healthcare, helping clinicians focus on patient care by automatically capturing, understanding, and structuring clinical conversations in real time.

Our product supports clinicians across the full care workflow, from capturing patient conversations and reviewing AI-generated documentation to coordinating follow-up actions and completing work across mobile and web.

We’re hiring a Full-Stack Product Engineer to build these experiences from end to end. You’ll work across our mobile and web applications, backend services, APIs, and AI-powered workflows, partnering closely with product, design, clinical, and AI teams.

This role is for an engineer who cares deeply about the people using the product. You think beyond whether a feature technically works to whether it is intuitive, responsive, trustworthy, and valuable in a real clinical environment. You’re comfortable moving through the stack to solve the whole problem, whether that means refining an interaction, designing an API, improving a data model, integrating an AI capability, or strengthening the system behind the experience.

Our mobile application is primarily built in Flutter, alongside web applications, browser-based surfaces, and backend services. Flutter experience is helpful but not required. We value strong product engineering judgment, full-stack versatility, and a track record of shipping high-quality user experiences.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and own high-impact product experiences from early exploration through launch, measurement, and iteration.

  • Develop new workflows for AI-native healthcare software, including:

    • Real-time transcription and ambient documentation

    • AI-assisted review, editing, and clinical workflows

    • Multimodal inputs and intelligent recommendations

    • Agentic actions that help clinicians complete work

    • Collaborative and cross-device workflows

    • Offline and low-connectivity experiences

  • Work across mobile, web, backend services, and APIs to deliver cohesive end-to-end experiences.

  • Partner closely with clinicians, product managers, and designers to understand real-world problems and translate them into simple, thoughtful products.

  • Collaborate with AI engineers to bring model capabilities into production in ways that are responsive, understandable, and trustworthy.

  • Design data models, APIs, and service boundaries that support fast product iteration and reliable user experiences.

  • Build polished interfaces across our Flutter mobile application and web-based surfaces.

  • Own the quality of what you ship, including usability, performance, accessibility, analytics, testing, observability, and release readiness.

  • Improve shared systems and product foundations when they unlock faster or better development, including:

    • Reusable application components and interaction patterns

    • State management and data-fetching primitives

    • Networking, caching, and synchronization

    • Background processing and resilient workflows

    • APIs, services, and asynchronous jobs

    • Logging, monitoring, and product diagnostics

  • Prototype quickly, learn from real usage, and refine experiences using qualitative and quantitative feedback.

  • Help shape product and technical strategy as the Ambient AI product line grows.

  • Mentor other engineers and raise the bar for engineering quality, product thinking, and craft across the team.

What You Have

  • Professional software development experience, with significant ownership of user-facing products or features.

  • Strong experience building applications across multiple parts of the stack, such as mobile or web clients, backend services, APIs, databases, and cloud infrastructure.

  • A track record of taking ambiguous product ideas through technical design, implementation, launch, and iteration.

  • Strong product judgment and attention to interaction quality, usability, performance, and craft.

  • Experience building polished frontend experiences using a modern mobile or web framework.

  • Experience designing and operating backend services, APIs, and data models in production.

  • Comfort moving through the stack to solve the most important product or user problem.

  • Strong understanding of software architecture, testing, observability, reliability, and maintainability.

  • Experience collaborating closely with product, design, backend, data, or AI teams.

  • An understanding that reliability, latency, and data integrity are fundamental parts of the user experience.

  • An ownership mindset and bias for action. You identify important problems, create clarity, and drive work through completion.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building AI-native, conversational, agentic, or real-time product experiences.

  • Experience with Flutter and Dart or another cross-platform mobile framework.

  • Experience building modern web applications with JavaScript or TypeScript.

  • Experience integrating large language models, transcription systems, or other machine-learning services into production products.

  • Experience with audio or video capture, streaming, transcription, or long-running media workflows.

  • Experience with offline-first applications, background sync, resilient local persistence, or conflict handling.

  • Experience designing event-driven systems, asynchronous workflows, or real-time data pipelines.

  • Familiarity with product analytics, experimentation, and measuring feature adoption or usability.

  • Experience with performance optimization, observability, CI/CD, and release automation.

  • Native iOS or Android experience when platform-specific capabilities are needed.

  • Exposure to healthcare, HIPAA, SOC 2, privacy, security, or other regulated environments.

  • Experience with Chrome extensions or workflows that span mobile, browser, and web applications.

Why Join

  • Build a product that directly gives clinicians more time to focus on their patients.

  • Own meaningful problems across the complete product stack, from user interaction to backend execution.

  • Create new product experiences at the intersection of AI, healthcare, mobile, and the web.

  • Work across the full product lifecycle, from understanding user needs to shipping and improving the experience.

  • Solve distinctive engineering challenges involving real-time audio, multimodal AI, offline behavior, agentic workflows, and sensitive clinical data.

  • Have meaningful influence over product direction, technical architecture, and engineering culture.

  • Join at a stage where individual engineers can shape both what we build and how we build it.

  • Grow into broader product, technical, or engineering leadership as the team and platform expand.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.

Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

This is not a conventional scope management role. You'll serve as the decision-maker and process architect for every request that falls outside standard product boundaries, fielding escalations from Sales, Operations, and Account Management, evaluating feasibility and business fit, and driving fast, defensible resolutions. You'll sit at the intersection of product, operations, and customer service, holding the line on scope while remaining a trusted partner to the business and building the systems that make both possible at scale.

You'll own EHR Credentialing operations across a team of four, mapping workflows end-to-end, eliminating manual and error-prone steps through automation, and tracking the metrics that matter: cycle time, error rate, backlog size, and automation coverage. In parallel, you'll provide the operational backbone for Business Operations, owning onboarding, offboarding, and documentation management workflows to ensure ongoing compliance.

Across all of it, you'll be the process architect codifying exceptions triage, credentialing, and BizOps workflows into documented playbooks, leveraging AI tools and internal platforms like Retool and Vercel to eliminate manual work, and establishing the team's operating cadence through weekly reviews, SLA reports, and cross-functional syncs.

Required

  • 5–8 years in operations, product operations, or technical operations

  • ideally in high-growth SaaS or healthcare technology with demonstrated experience owning cross-functional processes that required triage, judgment, and stakeholder alignment

  • Experience managing a small team, setting priorities, tracking output, and holding people accountable to SLAs while balancing competing commercial and operational needs

  • Hands-on experience with SQL and BI or internal tooling platforms (Looker Studio, Retool, Power BI, Tableau, or similar) to build reporting that stakeholders actually use

  • Strong process design instincts and you think in systems, document them clearly, and build playbooks that survive personnel changes

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication: equally fluent writing policy documents, exception recommendations, and executive summaries

Preferred

  • Background in healthcare technology, EHR systems, or clinical workflow operations with familiarity in the credentialing landscape

  • Experience in BizOps, GTM Ops, or Revenue Operations supporting Sales or Account Management teams, ideally at the boundary between Product and commercial functions

  • Familiarity with AI tools and LLMs for automating repetitive workflows, and enough experience with low-code platforms like Retool or Vercel to collaborate effectively with technical builders

  • Obsessively organized but adaptable - you hold complex portfolios without losing the thread when priorities shift, and you manage upward proactively without being asked

  • A systems thinker and low-ego operator who translates process needs into scalable solutions and builds trust through consistent follow-through

  • Someone who can say no clearly and fairly with a documented reason and make high-stakes, manual processes clean, transparent, and repeatable

 - Strong process design instincts and you think in systems, document them clearly, and build playbooks that survive personnel changes

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication: equally fluent writing policy documents, exception recommendations, and executive summaries

 - Background in healthcare technology, EHR systems, or clinical workflow operations with familiarity in the credentialing landscape

 - Experience in BizOps, GTM Ops, or Revenue Operations supporting Sales or Account Management teams, ideally at the boundary between Product and commercial functions

 - Familiarity with AI tools and LLMs for automating repetitive workflows, and enough experience with low-code platforms like Retool or Vercel to collaborate effectively with technical builders

 - Obsessively organized but adaptable - you hold complex portfolios without losing the thread when priorities shift, and you manage upward proactively without being asked

 - A systems thinker and low-ego operator who translates process needs into scalable solutions and builds trust through consistent follow-through

 - Someone who can say no clearly and fairly with a documented reason  and make high-stakes, manual processes clean, transparent, and repeatable

About the Role

We’re looking for a strategic and hands-on Senior People Business Partner to support Engineering, Product and Design. This role will partner closely with leaders to solve people and organizational challenges, strengthen manager effectiveness, and drive data-informed decisions across the employee lifecycle.

You’ll build relationships with the teams you support, identify issues before they become problems, and own work end to end. This is a role for someone comfortable operating across performance, compensation, retention, talent planning, employee relations, and organizational health without relying on layers of specialized teams. This is a hybrid role and requires 3 days per week in our Mountain View HQ. You’ll help shape our people strategy, support organizational growth, and deliver thoughtful, data-informed solutions that enhance the employee experience and drive business outcomes.

What You’ll Do

  • Serve as a hands-on People partner to leaders across organizational design, talent planning, team effectiveness, and workforce decisions

  • Coach managers on performance, feedback, career development, difficult conversations, and stronger day-to-day management practices

  • Partner on compensation and equity planning, including reviews, allocation decisions, internal consistency, and standardization

  • Use people data and business context to identify trends, risks, and opportunities across retention, performance, engagement, and talent

  • Develop and support retention strategies for critical talent and teams

  • Build strong relationships across the teams you support and proactively surface risks, opportunities, and organizational issues

  • Work across People, Finance, Legal, Talent, and business teams to move work forward and resolve issues

  • Build scalable processes that improve consistency, decision-making, and manager effectiveness

  • Maintain strong judgment, discretion, and confidentiality in all people-related matters

What You Have

  • 7+ years of progressive experience, including at least 3 years in an similar role

  • Experience supporting senior leaders in a high-growth, fast-paced, or mid size start up environment

  • Experienced with HR tools, automation, and AI, with the ability to build self-service resources, automate repeatable work, and create practical solutions that help managers move faster and operate more independently.

  • Exceptional organizational and project planning skills, with the ability to get into the details, create structure, align stakeholders, and drive work through completion.

  • Experience supporting and standardizing compensation, equity, performance, retention, talent management, and employee relations

  • Strong manager coaching skills and the ability to raise and reinforce management standards

  • Business acumen and the ability to use data to forecast problems and drive decisions

  • A track record of owning ambiguous problems through resolution.

  • Ability to operate independently, move quickly, and work across functions

  • Strong communication, judgment, and influencing skills across levels

  • Comfort moving between strategy, execution, and day-to-day problem solving

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

At Commure, the AI Integration Team plays a crucial role in supporting the company’s core products, Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) and Ambient, by ensuring seamless data flow between our platform and over 40 Electronic Medical Records (EMRs). This team is responsible for fetching vital Encounter and Appointment data from multiple EMRs and, when necessary, writing data back to these systems. The team's work ensures the interoperability and smooth exchange of healthcare data via HL7, enabling healthcare providers to deliver more efficient and accurate care while streamlining administrative processes. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who takes ownership end-to-end, moves fast, and wants their work to directly impact how care is delivered.

What You'll Do

  • Design and implement complex integration solutions between our platform and third-party healthcare systems (EHRs, insurance providers, etc.) while ensuring high performance, reliability, and scalability.

  • Utilize the latest developments in LLM technology to automate the reverse-engineering of electronic health records.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (product, engineering, and healthcare) to gather integration requirements, define technical approaches, and prioritize tasks based on business needs.

  • Contribute to the technical direction of the integration platform by proposing and implementing improvements to architecture, tools, and technologies.

  • Take ownership of end-to-end integration workflows, from design and development through to deployment and post-launch monitoring.

  • Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, troubleshoot integration issues, and proactively improve the reliability of integrations in production environments.

  • Ensure all integration work adheres to healthcare compliance and security standards (e.g., HIPAA, HL7, FHIR) and collaborate with security teams to protect sensitive data.

  • Work closely with junior engineers to provide technical guidance and mentorship, helping them solve problems and ensuring high-quality code standards are followed.

  • Drive the implementation of best practices for integration development, including testing, error handling, version control, and continuous integration.

  • Collaborate with DevOps and QA teams to implement monitoring and alerting systems that ensure integration reliability and system health in production.

  • Stay up-to-date with industry trends in healthcare technology, integration patterns, and emerging tools, continuously suggesting and applying innovations that can improve system performance and integration capabilities.

  • Participate in agile development cycles, contributing to sprint planning, retrospectives, and maintaining a collaborative and efficient working environment

What You Have

  • [Required] Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent extensive experience

  • 5+ years of professional software development industry experience

  • Proficiency in backend languages like Python, Go, or C++.

  • Proficiency in frontend languages like Javascript, HTML, CSS

  • Experience including but not limited to Git, GCP / AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, relational and non-relational DBs, and monitoring/alerting tools

  • Proven track record of designing and implementing end-to-end solutions and making successful architectural decisions

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

About the Role:

We’re looking for a builder - someone who loves solving hard operational problems with code, data, and product intuition. You are right for this role if you’re someone who can take an operational workflow, inspect the data, understand the business logic, build and modify tools, evaluate outcomes and ship measurable improvements. Part consultant, part product thinker, part data analyst, you’ll help us automate and scale traditionally manual workflows that underpin healthcare operations - from claim submissions to payment posting.

This role sits at the intersection of product, data, and implementation. You’ll design, test, and operationalize automations across our stack, work hands-on with Product, Engineering teams, and our customers to map and rebuild their workflows, and create systems that scale. You’ll be accountable for outcomes - building the infrastructure, tools, and processes that let our teams and our clients move faster and smarter.

We want people who are excellent operators, strong problem solvers, and comfortable building from scratch.

At Commure, there are no speed limits in your growth. If you show ownership and deliver results, your responsibilities - and impact - will grow rapidly. We value people who move fast, think deeply, take pride in solid execution, and deliver results for our customers.

This full-time position requires working 5 days a week in our Mountain View, CA office.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own high-impact processes: Own one or more automation surfaces end-to-end: instrumentation, workflow mapping, SQL/data analysis, tool changes, experiment evaluation, rollout, monitoring, and post-launch debugging.

  • Design and automate workflows: Use SQL, APIs, scripts, and emerging tools (including LLMs and harnesses) to automate manual claim-related workflows and improve scalability

  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with Product, Engineering, and Account Management to influence roadmap priorities and scale successful solutions

  • Analyze and optimize: Build dashboards and reporting pipelines to monitor productivity, quality, and financial outcomes; identify bottlenecks and automate fixes

 

What You Bring

  • 2+ years of experience in operations, consulting, or data-heavy roles at a tech company or fast-paced startup

  • Strong SQL fluency - comfortable querying, analyzing, and structuring data to drive insights and automation

  • Excellent problem-solving and systems-thinking skills; able to diagnose root causes and design scalable solutions

  • Proven ability to manage complex projects end-to-end, working autonomously in ambiguous, fast-changing environments

  • Bonus: Experience with AI Automation Infrastructure, such as:

    • Prompt Iteration

    • Evaluations

    • Failure Analysis

    • Agent Workflows

    • Hallucination / Leakage / Overfitting Risks

    • Human-in-the-Loop Design

    • Confidence Thresholds

    • Auditability

    • Production Monitoring

  • Bonus: Experience in healthcare operations, claims, or billing systems

  • Bonus: Experience building or integrating workflows via APIs, Python, or web automation tools (Zapier, Retool, custom scripts, etc.)

  • Bonus: Experience with agentic workflow development, building orchestration scripts and validation scripts, and working with the cloud

 

Who You Are

  • You investigate metric drops relentlessly until you've identified a root cause.

  • You validate dashboard queries before trusting the output.

  • You work comfortably with raw logs, database records, and edge cases.

  • You translate domain expert knowledge into scalable automation.

  • You apply rigorous critical thinking to LLM outputs and build appropriate guardrails.

  • You ship useful tools early and iterate rather than over-engineer a perfect design doc.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer for our R&D team at Commure, the team taking emerging technology from inception to impact. We scout new capabilities — a frontier LLM that can chain tool calls, browser agents that can navigate the web, new agent harnesses that can self improve — and figure out how to productionize them for healthcare. Our job is the full arc: research the technology, productize it, deliver it to customers, and own it as a P&L until it graduates.

Graduation has taken the following shapes in the past:

  • Embedded into an existing product — e.g., the AI Copilot in our practice management suite.

  • Becomes its own product — e.g., Air, the EHR.

  • Becomes an internal RCM workflow that saves the company millions annually — e.g., EOB web agents and appeal agents.

This role will be hybrid and based in our Mountain View or San Francisco offices.

What You'll Do

  • Build the infrastructure that orchestrates, evaluates, and runs sub-agents, including the channel adapters that intelligence flows through

  • Get hands-on with the cutting edge — chaining tool calls across LLMs, deploying browser agents, building self-improving harnesses — and turn experimental prototypes into production-level tools and products

  • Take a technology from first principles to production: research it, build it into a product, ship it to customers, and own it through graduation to something bigger

  • Establish best practices for code quality, testing, deployment, and observability

  • Collaborate with product managers, designers, and clinical experts to ship intuitive solutions that work in real clinical environments

  • Be part of a fast-moving team that celebrates large ambition, ships daily, and makes decisions quickly

What You Have

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience, required

  • Professional software engineering experience, ideally in a high-growth or startup environment

  • Strong fullstack skills — Python on the backend (required), Javascript/React on the frontend, with working knowledge of containers and cloud (Docker, Kubernetes)

  • Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs or building AI-powered features in production

  • Track record of driving work from early ideation to successful production deployment

  • Strong debugging and problem-solving skills with a history of demonstrated resourcefulness

  • Strong communication skills — comfortable working with both engineers and non-technical stakeholders including clinical teams

  • Experience in fast-moving environments where shipping quickly is the norm

About the Role

The Director of Compliance is responsible for designing, overseeing, and monitoring the effectiveness of Commure, Inc.’s corporate compliance program. This role is critical in promoting a culture of integrity and ensuring the company adheres to the complex web of laws, regulations, and standards governing the Health IT industry. This role will function as an independent and objective leader, reviewing and evaluating compliance issues throughout the organization. They will monitor systems and processes to ensure compliance with all applicable healthcare laws, data privacy regulations, and company policies, including the Code of Conduct.

 

The Director of Compliance will report directly to the Chief Legal Officer and dotted line to the Board of Directors (the Board), ensuring independence and authority. This role will serve as a key advisor to senior leadership and a resource for all employees, providing guidance on the company’s ethical values and facilitating compliant and integral business operations.

What You'll Do

The key accountabilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Knows, understands, and champions Commure’s mission, vision, and values through leadership behaviors, practices, and decisions.

  • Chairs the Corporate Compliance Committee, ensuring regular meetings with appropriate cross-functional representation from Legal, Human Resources, Engineering, Product, Security, and Sales.

  • Develops, implements, and maintains policies, procedures, and controls for the compliance program to prevent and detect illegal, unethical, or improper conduct, with a strong focus on Health IT-specific risks.

  • Conducts regular, comprehensive risk assessments to identify potential areas of compliance vulnerability, including those related to HIPAA/HITECH, data security, the Anti-Kickback Statute, Stark Law, information blocking, and FDA regulations for Software as a Medical Device (SaMD).

  • Develops, implements, and tracks corrective action plans to resolve compliance issues, providing guidance to prevent future occurrences.

  • Establishes and executes an annual compliance work plan based on risk assessment results, including targeted auditing and monitoring activities.

  • Develops and reports on key compliance metrics and data analytics to senior leadership and the Audit Committee of the Board, detecting potential fraud, waste, abuse, and other aberrant patterns.

  • Directs and oversees the creation and delivery of effective compliance training and educational materials for all employees, executives, board members, and key vendors, focusing on the real-world application of compliance principles to Commure's business model.

  • Manages and promotes effective lines of communication, including the company’s compliance hotline, ensuring a safe and anonymous channel for reporting concerns.

  • Monitors the performance and effectiveness of the compliance program on an ongoing basis and implements continuous improvements.

  • Maintains expert knowledge of the evolving healthcare regulatory landscape and advises the company on the potential impact of new laws and regulations.

  • Liaises with senior management to ensure a strong "tone at the top," integrate compliance activities into business operations, and evaluate the compliance-related performance of employees.

 

What You Have

  • Bachelor’s degree required; Juris Doctorate (JD) or relevant Master’s degree (e.g., MBA, MHA) is strongly preferred.

  • Certification in Healthcare Compliance (CHC) or similar compliance certification is highly desirable.

  • A minimum of 6-10 years of experience in a healthcare regulatory and compliance role, with experience in a leadership capacity, preferably within a Health IT, SaaS, or medical device company.

  • Proven ability to develop and implement effective compliance policies, procedures, and training programs.

  • Expert knowledge of the U.S. healthcare regulatory landscape, including deep expertise in HIPAA, HITECH, the Anti-Kickback Statute, and state/federal data privacy laws (e.g., CCPA/CPRA).

  • Demonstrated experience with FDA regulations for digital health tools or Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and ONC Cures Act Final Rule requirements (including information blocking and interoperability) is a significant plus.

  • Exceptional leadership and management skills with the ability to motivate and influence others positively.

  • Superior verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex regulatory concepts to a variety of audiences.

  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build collaborative relationships across all levels of the organization.

  • Excellent organizational and strategic planning skills.

  • A deep commitment to fostering teamwork and continuous quality improvement.

  • Analytical and strategic thinker with strong problem-solving capabilities.

  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, innovative tech environment.

About the Role

The Director of Compliance is responsible for designing, overseeing, and monitoring the effectiveness of Commure, Inc.’s corporate compliance program. This role is critical in promoting a culture of integrity and ensuring the company adheres to the complex web of laws, regulations, and standards governing the Health IT industry. This role will function as an independent and objective leader, reviewing and evaluating compliance issues throughout the organization. They will monitor systems and processes to ensure compliance with all applicable healthcare laws, data privacy regulations, and company policies, including the Code of Conduct.

 

The Director of Compliance will report directly to the Chief Legal Officer and dotted line to the Board of Directors (the Board), ensuring independence and authority. This role will serve as a key advisor to senior leadership and a resource for all employees, providing guidance on the company’s ethical values and facilitating compliant and integral business operations.

 - Knows, understands, and champions Commure’s mission, vision, and values through leadership behaviors, practices, and decisions.

 - Chairs the Corporate Compliance Committee, ensuring regular meetings with appropriate cross-functional representation from Legal, Human Resources, Engineering, Product, Security, and Sales.

 - Develops, implements, and maintains policies, procedures, and controls for the compliance program to prevent and detect illegal, unethical, or improper conduct, with a strong focus on Health IT-specific risks.

 - Conducts regular, comprehensive risk assessments to identify potential areas of compliance vulnerability, including those related to HIPAA/HITECH, data security, the Anti-Kickback Statute, Stark Law, information blocking, and FDA regulations for Software as a Medical Device (SaMD).

 - Establishes and executes an annual compliance work plan based on risk assessment results, including targeted auditing and monitoring activities.

 - Monitors the performance and effectiveness of the compliance program on an ongoing basis and implements continuous improvements.

 - Proven ability to develop and implement effective compliance policies, procedures, and training programs.

 - Exceptional leadership and management skills with the ability to motivate and influence others positively.

 - Superior verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex regulatory concepts to a variety of audiences.

 - Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build collaborative relationships across all levels of the organization.

 - Excellent organizational and strategic planning skills.

 - A deep commitment to fostering teamwork and continuous quality improvement.

 - Analytical and strategic thinker with strong problem-solving capabilities.

 - Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, innovative tech environment.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We're hiring a Software Engineer II to join Air Billing, the team behind the highest-traffic surfaces in our practice management product: claims, appointments, and payments posting — the workspaces billers and practice staff live in all day.

These aren't basic CRUD screens. They're fast, data-dense, keyboard-driven workflows over millions of claims, sitting on real healthcare plumbing (EDI transactions, payer automations). AI is central to how we drive productivity, but we don't solve everything with an agent — we put LLMs in the loop only where day-to-day friction is highest.

We're mid-way through a generational rebuild of these surfaces, and there's an enormous amount to build: rebuilding the claims workspace, making bulk operations safe over tens of thousands of records, stitching together a unified claim activity timeline, and putting AI to work where billers feel the most friction. As a Software Engineer II, you'll own end-to-end features across this work and see them run in production for billers every day.

You'll join a small, tight-knit team that owns the claims, appointments, and eligibility surfaces end-to-end. It's a hands-on group that ships fast, reviews each other's work closely, and sits right next to the billing operators who use what we build — so you'll see the impact of your features in days, not quarters. You'll work alongside senior engineers who'll help you go deep on the domain and grow into bigger problems over time — and, as the team scales, take a growing hand in setting the technical standards and direction we all build on.

What You’ll Do

  • Own features end-to-end on the claims, appointments, and payments-posting surfaces — from design phase through production rollout

  • Write production-ready code with meaningful tests and observability, and design clean interfaces and data models that hold up as the surfaces grow

  • Partner with product, design, and billing operations to make sure what you ship actually solves the biller's workflow problem

  • Build reliability and observability into your features — dashboards, logging, and alerting that make production issues fast to catch and root-cause

  • Review code and designs with an eye toward correctness, performance on data-dense screens, and a consistent user experience

  • Help set the technical standards and direction the team builds on as we scale — shaping component patterns, API and data-fetching conventions, and testing and observability practices, and helping onboard and level up teammates

What You Have

  • 3+ years building full-stack applications, with a track record of shipping features end-to-end in production

  • Solid frontend skills — you build clean, maintainable UIs and can diagnose and fix common rendering issues in data-dense screens

  • API and data-layer fundamentals — you can build backend endpoints handling filtering and pagination over sizable datasets, and reason about the queries behind them

  • Sound technical judgment for feature-level work — you evaluate tradeoffs, escalate risks appropriately, and avoid over-engineering

  • Good debugging and observability instincts — comfortable with monitoring, logging, and alerting

  • Clear communication — you keep teammates and partners informed, and ask questions early when things are unclear

  • Ownership mindset and bias for action — you take responsibility for your features and follow through with urgency and customer focus

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with healthcare billing data — EDI X12 (270/271, 276/277, 835, 837), clearinghouses, ERAs/EOBs, denial codes — or a demonstrated ability to ramp on a gnarly domain quickly

  • Experience shipping LLM-powered features into production workflows, not just demos

  • Exposure to analytical/OLAP stores alongside a transactional database

  • Strong product intuition and a track record of influencing UX/UI decisions to improve usability

  • Experience working in regulated industries (healthcare, finance, insurance) with attention to security and compliance

About the Role

The Data Integrations team owns the systems that move clinical and financial data between Commure and hundreds of external healthcare endpoints. The domain is EMRs, but the engineering problem is distributed systems at scale: durable orchestration on Temporal, strong delivery semantics against unreliable third parties, and a data and networking substrate that has to keep up as the business grows.

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to set technical direction for this platform and help us scale as we more towards Enterprise Customers.

What You’ll Do

  • Set the technical direction for the platform. Decide what we build and how we execute.

  • Own the architecture of the systems that move data through our platform, the orchestration layer, the pipelines, the data stores, and evolve them as scale.

  • Look ahead. Anticipate the scaling and reliability walls we'll hit two and four quarters out, and get in front of them before they become incidents.

  • Set the bar for observability and operational readiness (monitoring, logging, distributed tracing, dashboards, alerting, SLOs, and safe production rollouts) and make sure the team actually lives by it.

  • Work hand-in-hand with platform and product teams to keep sensitive customer data protected, tighten security boundaries, and stay on top of our regulatory and compliance obligations.

  • Own complex, cross-system initiatives end to end: architecture and design, implementation, migration, rollout, and everything that comes with running it in production.

  • Make pragmatic calls that weigh security, correctness, reliability, performance, and simplicity against how fast we need to ship.

  • Mentor Senior and Staff engineers, run architecture and design reviews, and push the technical bar higher through clear direction, strong engineering habits, and honest feedback.

  • Take real ownership in a fast-moving environment. Spot systemic risks early and fix the root cause instead of patching around it.

What You Have

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent extensive experience

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a substantial chunk at Staff-equivalent scope: architectural decisions on multi-quarter projects, made under real constraints, that you'd still defend today.

  • Deep experience building and operating distributed systems at scale, high-throughput pipelines, data-intensive services. You can talk about the non-obvious failure modes, not just the happy path.

  • Strong data-layer and concurrency judgment. You've made a relational database (Postgres or similar) do more than it wanted to, and you know when to reach for a DB lock, when Redis is the right tool, and when the right move is a design that doesn't need either.

  • Real depth in the boring-but-critical layers. Networking and egress (NAT, static IPs, connection lifecycle, DNS, TLS), the database, the container runtime. You've been the person the org turns to when something below the application layer is misbehaving.

  • Production experience with GCP and container orchestration (Kubernetes, Knative, or similar serverless-on-k8s), and fluency in a modern backend language (Python strongly preferred; Go or similar is a plus).

  • The ability to translate business goals into technical direction, and technical tradeoffs into language non-engineers can act on.

  • A history of leveling up the engineers around you.

Bonus if you have

  • Healthcare integrations experience — HL7 v2, FHIR, and EHRs like Epic, Cerner, or Athenahealth. We can teach the domain; we're hiring for the systems judgment above.

  • Experience with the compliance envelope this work lives inside (HIPAA, SOC 2) and the security posture that comes with handling PHI.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to own the accounts and ledgering spine of our RCM platform. This is the path from "insurance paid us" to "the books balance, the patient knows what they owe, and leadership can trust the numbers."

The team is designing and building the next generation of our account and ledgering system. We're moving toward an event-oriented financial model where every charge, payment, adjustment, and refund is immutable. Balances get derived from history rather than maintained by hand. Reporting should fall out of the design, not be stitched together afterward.

Your team owns the full money path:

  • The insurance ledger append-only entries recording payer payments, contractual adjustments, denials, and patient responsibility buckets per procedure, with reversal/refund chains for corrections

  • Posting and adjustment engines that turn remittances into ledger entries and automatically write off, rebucket, or transfer amounts to patient responsibility based on customer rules

  • Patient account ledgers tracking balance, payments, credits, and refunds that drive statements, the patient portal, and collections

  • Bank reconciliation — matching insurer checks to actual bank deposits (via bank APIs, BAI2 files, OCR'd deposit slips) so we only post against verified dollars

  • Reporting ledger and AR — procedure-level rollups, point-in-time views, AR aging, collections reports, plus drift detection when operational balances disagree with reports

  • An emerging unified event stream that will become the backbone of a cleaner, replayable ledger architecture

What You’ll Do

  • Design the next-generation account and ledger model, immutable events, derived balances, clear semantics around payer balance vs. patient balance vs. adjustments vs. cash, with invariants that make it structurally impossible to "print money"

  • Keep operational balances and financial reports in lockstep. Posting, adjustments, patient balances, rollups, and balance reports need to agree. When they don't, we need drift detection and self-healing

  • Reconcile three (or four) sources of truth: billed charges, payer remittances, bank deposits, and financial reports. Surface discrepancies before customers do

  • Scale idempotent, explainable posting and adjustment pipelines across high transaction volumes using negation/reversal semantics instead of mutable edits

  • Operate money-critical systems on very large Postgres tables, safe migrations, trigger-driven projections, backfills, observability, and incident response where "eventually consistent" isn't acceptable

  • Set the bar for observability and operational readiness (monitoring, logging, distributed tracing, dashboards, alerting, SLOs, and safe production rollouts) and make sure the team actually lives by it.

  • Work hand-in-hand with platform and product teams to keep sensitive customer data protected, tighten security boundaries, and stay on top of our regulatory and compliance obligations.

  • Own complex, cross-system initiatives end to end: architecture and design, implementation, migration, rollout, and everything that comes with running it in production.

  • Make pragmatic calls that weigh security, correctness, reliability, performance, and simplicity against how fast we need to ship.

  • Mentor Senior and Staff engineers, run architecture and design reviews, and push the technical bar higher through clear direction, strong engineering habits, and honest feedback.

  • Take real ownership in a fast-moving environment. Spot systemic risks early and fix the root cause instead of patching around it.

What You Have

  • 8+ years building software, with a track record of Staff-level work, architecture ownership, mentoring, cross-team influence

  • Strong backend engineering (Python preferred) and deep experience with relational databases at scale: query performance, ACID transactions, safe migrations, data integrity

  • Real experience designing or operating financial systems, payments, billing, reconciliation, accounting, or ledgers. You get double-entry accounting, append-only ledgers, idempotency, reversals, and why balances need to be derived from immutable history

  • You've shipped production systems with observability, alerting, and incident response practices, especially for high-stakes workflows

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills. You can work with ops and customers when correctness matters

Bonus points if you have

  • Healthcare RCM, patient accounting, insurance remittance (835/ERA), AR aging, or practice-management billing

  • File-based integrations, bank reconciliation, event-sourced/CDC architectures, or high-throughput batch pipelines

  • Experience evolving a monolith toward clearer domain boundaries or event-oriented model

jobs.descriptionHtml:

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role
This is not a conventional support or project management role. You'll serve as the operational owner for Ambient EHR integrations across our enterprise health system portfolio, acting as the connective tissue between Engineering, Implementation Consultants, Customer Success, and client IT teams. When an integration breaks, stalls, or behaves unexpectedly, you're the person who diagnoses what's actually happening, routes it to the right owner with the right context, and drives it to a fast, defensible resolution.

What You'll Do

You'll own integration launch coordination end-to-end for new enterprise deployments, from kickoff and technical validation through go-live and stabilization, across a portfolio of 10+ EHRs. This includes account configuration and validation, provider and site setup verification, sync health monitoring, and coordinating client-side dependencies like network access, API credentials, and template builds.

You'll be the triage engine for integration issues in production: reproducing and scoping problems, distinguishing product bugs from configuration issues from client-environment problems, and holding the line on triage SLAs. You'll work directly in internal tooling, tracking issues in Linear, and you'll build the dashboards and health metrics that give leadership visibility into enterprise sync rates and error trends.

Across all of it, you'll be the process architect: codifying integration triage, launch, and escalation workflows into documented runbooks and playbooks that survive personnel changes, and establishing operating cadence through weekly status reporting to executive audiences, SLA reviews, and cross-functional syncs.

What You Have

Required:

  • 8-10 years in operations, ideally in healthcare technology with demonstrated experience owning cross-functional workflows requiring triage, judgment, and stakeholder alignment

  • Proven triage and escalation ownership: you can reproduce an issue, isolate root cause across product, configuration, and client environment, and route it with enough context that engineering doesn't have to re-investigate

  • Strong documentation instincts: you think in systems, write runbooks that others can execute without you, and keep them current

  • Strong written communication, equally fluent in executive status updates, internal escalation summaries, and client-facing emails to health system IT and clinical stakeholders

  • A systems thinker and low-ego operator who builds trust through consistent follow-through, and who can deliver a clear, documented "no" when a request falls outside supported scope

Nice to Have:

  • Direct experience with ambient AI clinical documentation workflows or point-of-care technology deployments

  • Hands-on experience with at least one major EHR platform (Epic, Meditech Expanse, Athena, Cerner, eClinicalWorks, or oncology EMRs)

  • Working knowledge of EHR integration fundamentals: HL7, FHIR, REST APIs, token-based authentication, and the practical failure modes of each (auth errors, network/firewall blocks, data routing issues)

  • Experience coordinating launches with enterprise health system IT teams, including navigating network access, SSID/firewall constraints, credentialing, and third-party template vendors

  • Obsessively organized but adaptable: you hold a complex multi-client portfolio without losing the thread when priorities shift, and you manage upward proactively without being asked

  • Investigate production failures, identify root causes, and improve the reliability of the overall system.

What You Have

  • Professional experience building and operating production software systems.

  • Strong proficiency in Python, including experience developing APIs and services with FastAPI.

  • Strong full-stack development skills, with experience building modern applications using React and JavaScript or TypeScript.

  • Experience designing data models and production systems with PostgreSQL.

  • Hands-on experience building with LLMs, AI agents, or agent harnesses, including concepts such as tool calling, orchestration, context management, evaluations, retries, and human-in-the-loop workflows.

  • A strong understanding of production engineering, including testing, observability, alerting, incident response, and system reliability.

  • Experience with containers and cloud infrastructure, such as Docker and Kubernetes.

  • The ability to move quickly while maintaining a high bar for correctness, maintainability, and user experience.

  • Strong product judgment and an instinct for simplifying complex operational workflows.

  • Excellent ownership and communication skills, including the ability to work directly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • A builder mindset and excitement about applying AI to high-impact healthcare problems.

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience building email agents, support automation, workflow engines, or other asynchronous processing systems.

  • Experience building systems that require strong auditability, security, and data privacy.

  • Experience operating high-volume distributed systems with queues, background workers, and third-party integrations.

Now we need a Talent leader who can match the pace of what we're building and raise the bar on who we bring in to build it.

The gap between the people you hire and their impact on patient care is immediate here. That's what makes this hard. It's also what makes it worth doing.

If you're energized by high stakes, high standards, and a company operating at the edge of what healthcare technology can do, this is the role!

What You'll Do

  • Own the full talent function end-to-end from headcount planning and sourcing strategy through offer close and onboarding handoff ensuring Commure consistently hires the people who raise the bar

  • Partner directly with the CEO and senior leadership to translate business priorities into hiring plans, pipeline targets, and talent strategies that scale with the company's growth trajectory

  • Lead, build, and develop a high-performing global recruiting team, setting standards, coaching execution, and creating an environment where recruiters do the best work

  • Define and enforce what great looks like at Commure building structured interview frameworks, calibration processes, and scorecards that drive consistent, high-quality hiring decisions across every function

  • Own employer brand and candidate experience from first touch to first day ensuring every candidate interaction reflects the quality, speed, and integrity of how Commure operates

  • Build and maintain the recruiting infrastructure that scales ATS configuration, sourcing tools, offer strategy, compensation benchmarking, and the operational processes that keep a high-velocity team running without breaking

  • Drive recruiting analytics and reporting to senior leadership, tracking pipeline health, time-to-fill, quality of hire, offer acceptance rates, and source effectiveness to make real-time investment decisions

  • Identify and close top passive talent across EPD, GTM, Clinical, and G&A -personally leading searches for the most senior and strategic hires while enabling the team to execute across the full req load

What You Have:

  • 12+ years in talent acquisition with at least 5 years leading and managing a recruiting function/team at a high-growth technology company or relevant experience

  • Demonstrated experience scaling a team through a high-velocity growth period

  • Track record hiring across EPD, GTM, G&A and clinical or healthcare-adjacent functions

  • 5+ years of people management experience

  • Experience building or significantly rebuilding recruiting infrastructure, ATS, process, tooling, and team

  • Prior experience at a health tech, digital health, or enterprise SaaS company strongly preferred

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

We are seeking a Business Intelligence Engineer to support our Global Operations department in scaling the infrastructure for our core product lines (including Ambient Assist and Ambient Live). This role sits squarely at the intersection of software engineering, data architecture, and business operations. You will step beyond traditional analytics to design, build, and deploy custom internal applications, automated workflows, and robust ETL pipelines that power our day-to-day business execution.

Working within modern development environments (including Retool, Vercel, and custom API integrations), you will be a core driver in process and application implementation, migrating away from legacy tools, centralizing our technical operations solutions. The ideal candidate will either have a Software Engineering background with a strong pivot into Analytics, or an Analytics/Data Engineering background heavily supplemented by full-stack web development.

What You’ll Do

  • Application & Tooling Development: Build robust, interactive internal applications, custom front-end workflows, and automations (via platforms like Retool, Vercel, Cursor, or custom web apps) using advanced JavaScript and Python.

  • Data Pipeline Architecture: Design, write, and optimize complex SQL queries and data models to extract, manipulate, and aggregate data. Architect and maintain reliable ETL pipelines to support rapid operational scaling and AI/LLM integrations.

  • UI/UX Design & Development: Design intuitive, reliable UI/UX workflows that reduce manual effort for non-technical operators with a goal to simplify complexity without sacrificing capability.

  • Technical Governance & CI/CD: Strictly implement and adhere to version control and deployment pipelines (e.g., Git, GitHub PRs, Dev -> Release environments) to ensure all data products and front-end tools meet rigorous engineering QA standards.

  • Systems Implementation: Able to independently manage implementation of systems processes, enable automated workflows / CRONs, and set up centralized, scalable operational databases and applications.

  • Database & Schema Design: Apply advanced table design principles (normalization, indexing, key constraints) when building datasets or proposing schema changes to optimize performance across the data warehouse.

  • Process Automation: Develop automated scripts, webhooks, and API integrations that connect disparate data sources and streamline cross-functional business operations without manual oversight.

  • Cross-Functional Strategy: Act as a technical liaison between operations, product, and core data engineering teams to consolidate ambient data streams and enforce system reliability.

What You Have

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, or a highly related technical field.

  • 3+ years of professional experience in Software Engineering (with an analytics focus), Analytics Engineering, or Technical Operations.

  • Advanced proficiency in SQL and relational database architecture.

  • Strong programming skills in JavaScript and Python; proven experience building full-stack web solutions, APIs, or internal tooling.

  • Hands-on experience with version control (Git) and CI/CD workflows is strictly required.

  • Experience with internal tool builders (e.g., Retool) and modern deployment platforms (e.g., Vercel) is highly advantageous.

  • A proven track record of moving beyond basic dashboards to build functional, data-driven applications or automated infrastructure.

  • Systems-level thinker with a meticulous commitment to data accuracy, clean code, and robust technical documentation.

  • Excellent communication skills, capable of bridging the gap between deep technical engineering execution and high-level business strategy.

  • Self-motivated with a proactive approach to dismantling operational bottlenecks and standardizing best practices.

  • Highly adaptable in a fast-paced environment with a continuous stream of overlapping projects, capable of taking vague operational asks and translating them into precise technical execution.

Work Details:

  • Shift Detail: Night shift, (10:00 pm, BST - 7:00 am, BST)

  • Workdays: Monday to Friday

About the Role

We are looking for a driven and highly communicative Sales Development Representative (SDR) to join our growing Sales team in Bangladesh.

As an SDR, you will be responsible for creating new sales opportunities by identifying and engaging potential customers, understanding their needs, introducing them to our solutions, and booking qualified product demonstration meetings for our Account Executives. This is a high impact, target driven role where your ability to communicate confidently, build relationships, learn quickly, and persist through challenges will directly contribute to our sales growth. You will work closely with our US based Sales organization and collaborate with Account Executives to ensure qualified prospects are successfully transitioned into the next stage of the sales process.

What You'll Do

  • Research and identify potential customers and relevant decision makers within target organizations

  • Proactively engage prospects through phone calls, email, LinkedIn, and other appropriate outreach channels

  • Communicate clearly and confidently with prospective customers in English

  • Understand prospects’ business needs, challenges, and interests to determine whether they are a good fit for our solutions

  • Clearly communicate the value of our products and create interest in learning more

  • Schedule qualified product demonstrations and sales meetings for Account Executives

  • Follow up consistently with prospects who have expressed interest but are not yet ready to engage

  • Maintain accurate and timely records of prospect interactions, follow ups, and meeting outcomes in relevant sales systems

  • Provide Account Executives with relevant information about prospects before scheduled meetings

  • Collaborate closely with Account Executives and the broader Sales team to ensure a smooth handoff of qualified opportunities

  • Meet and work toward defined activity and performance targets, including prospect outreach, qualified meetings, and sales opportunities generated

  • Continuously learn and develop a strong understanding of our products, customers, market, and sales process

What You Have

  • Excellent verbal and written English communication skills

  • Strong interpersonal and conversational skills with the ability to confidently engage with customers

About the Role

Our team is a multidisciplinary group of visual communication designers, writers, motion designers, product designers, and producers building the way Commure shows up in the world. We partner closely with Product, Marketing, Growth, Clinical, Comms, and Executive teams to bring to life a complex, high-stakes category into work that feels compelling, human, and unmistakably ours.

We're looking for a Brand Design Lead to drive our brand expression and product creative across our most important moments: brand campaigns, product launches, in-product experiences, brand systems, and storytelling. This is a hands-on creative leadership role for someone with exceptional taste, care for craftsmanship, sharp strategic instincts, and the systems mindset to raise the quality of the work at scale. You're equally comfortable zooming out to define a cohesive creative vision and zooming in to sharpen a webpage, refine an illustration system, or direct a photoshoot. It is your job to set the quality bar and inspire our teams and our clients through communications design. We believe deeply in the power of in-person collaboration to accelerate the work and strengthen the team.

This role is based in our Mountain View office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

What You’ll Do

  • Define and lead the creative vision across brand and product: campaigns, launches, patient- and provider-facing experiences, in-product moments, event and executive storytelling, and the digital surfaces that connect them

  • Define our visual identity and design systems: typography, color, illustration, and the frameworks that keep our work coherent as we scale

  • Translate complex clinical and product subject matter into work that feels simple, human, and earns trust

  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Marketing, and Executive teams to shape brand and creative decisions

  • Set the quality bar for craft knowing when to push for a bigger idea and when to fight for the right color, type choice, or layout

  • Use AI tools thoughtfully in your workflow for concepting, prototyping, and production to move faster without compromising craft

What You Have

  • 7+ years of relevant experience in brand and visual design, with a track record of owning design end-to-end rather than primarily directing others

  • A strong portfolio showing range across brand identity, product design, and visual systems with clear examples of work you personally designed and shipped

  • Sophisticated visual craft, strong instincts across typography, color, composition, and layout

  • Experience building design systems that raise quality and consistency across a product or brand

  • Real fluency with AI tools and workflows (Midjourney, ComfyUI, generative video, LLMs for iteration) with concrete examples of how you've used them to move faster or improve quality

  • Comfort being the primary IC on brand and visual design today, with the interest and ability to hire and grow a team as scope expands

  • A systems-thinking approach and an eye for the details that matter

  • Deep empathy for the people we serve: patients, providers, caregivers and the judgment to hold that responsibility carefully in a regulated, high-trust category

jobs.title: Sales Engineer, Ambient AI
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About the Role

Commure Ambient is our Ambient AI platform. A clinician records the visit, and a finished note lands in their EHR, along with ICD codes, orders, a Patient 360 summary, and carried-forward history on supported systems. For a physician, that means charting is done when the visit is done.

Practices decide on Ambient by trying it: their own providers, their own patients, inside their own EHR. As a Sales Engineer on the Ambient team, you'll own those pilots from the first scoping call through a signed contract and hand-off to implementation.

This is a presales role. You'll partner with Account Executives on Commure Ambient pilots and on advanced AI pilots with healthcare practices: coding, orders, Patient 360, carry forward, and pre-visit summaries, running live inside ten EHRs (athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, AdvancedMD, ModMed, NextGen, Practice Fusion, WebPT, Prompt, iKnowMed, and Meditech Expanse). You'll typically have several pilots in flight at once, and you'll work closely with Engineering, our template team, and our implementation and operations teams to make each one succeed.

What You'll Do

  • Scope pilots. Lead the technical scoping call for each pilot, working directly with the providers who'll use Ambient and the decision makers evaluating it. Capture specialty, note types, EHR, and workflow, and turn it into a technical scope the deal can move forward on.

  • Build EHR integrations. Stand up the integration for each pilot across browser automation, DOM injection, and API paths. Our target from approved requests to a live integration the customer can use. When a note doesn't land in the chart, you'll find out why and fix it.

  • Bring advanced AI into the pilot. Confirm which beyond-the-note features the customer's EHR supports, configure them, and help providers put them to work: ICD coding, orders, Patient 360, carry forward, and pre-visit summaries.

  • Get templates right. Translate gold-standard notes and specialty requirements into template requests for our template engineering team, and triage template updates during the pilot on a 24-hour SLA.

  • Keep pilots healthy. Own the pilot Slack channel as the thread of record, triage in-pilot requests (template, integration, app feature) within 24 hours, and keep status and usage current in Salesforce so the AE always knows how the pilot is going.

  • Enable the sales team. Field integration and feature questions from AEs, help run the weekly integrations sales desk where engineering commitments to deals are made and tracked, and own the technical sections of RFPs and security questionnaires.

  • Hand off well. Deliver each new customer to implementation with the integration, templates, provider list, and known issues documented, so go-live picks up right where the pilot left off.

  • Make the team better. Escalate integration and product findings to Engineering with clear reproduction steps, and help build the tooling and playbook (debugging queries, checklists, wiki) that lets the next SE ramp faster than you did.

What Success Looks Like

  • Pilots start on the date we committed to the customer.

  • In-pilot issues are triaged within speed and urgency

  • Providers in your pilots are using Ambient, and where the EHR supports it, coding, carry forward, and Patient 360.

  • Your pilots convert, and implementation can pick up your hand-offs without rework.

What You Have

  • 3–7 years in sales engineering, solutions engineering, implementation, or healthcare IT. Engineers who want to spend more time with customers are welcome.

  • Hands-on experience with at least one ambulatory EHR (athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, AdvancedMD, NextGen, ModMed, Practice Fusion, WebPT). Epic, Cerner, or Meditech Expanse is a plus.

  • Comfort reading and debugging an integration: browser automation, DOM, REST APIs, JSON schemas, HL7/FHIR. You can use SQL and internal tooling to figure out why a note didn't land.

  • The ability to explain to a physician or technical teams how ambient AI builds a note, where it can miss, and what to do about it, in plain language.

  • Strong organization. You can juggle several pilots across multiple EHRs, keep Salesforce current, use Slack as your thread of record, and write updates that are short and specific.

  • Healthcare fluency: clinical documentation, specialty workflows, HIPAA, and the security questionnaires (SOC 2, HITRUST) that come with selling into practices.

  • A strong sense of ownership. Pilots launch on an SE's approval, and you take that responsibility seriously.

What We Offer

  • Live pilots from your first weeks, with providers using what you built.

  • Work at the frontier: LLM-generated notes, codes, and orders landing in production EHRs at real practices, every week.

  • A close working relationship with Product and Engineering. What you learn from customers shapes what we build next.

  • Documented SLAs, a written playbook, and a team that helps you ramp.

  • A clear path into Forward Deployed Engineering, enterprise Sales Engineering, or Product.

  • Competitive compensation and benefits.

Please be aware that all official communication from us will come exclusively from email addresses ending in @commure.com. Any emails from other domains are not affiliated with our organization.


Employees will act in accordance with the organization’s information security policies, to include but not limited to protecting assets from unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, destruction or interference nor execute particular security processes or activities. Employees will report to the information security office any confirmed or potential events or other risks to the organization. Employees will be required to attest to these requirements upon hire and on an annual basis.
